My starting routine
The same 4 steps for every question
READ
What is given? Read the Note too.
MARK
Underline what is asked. Number the clues.
DRAW
Sketch the shape. Label its faces or sides.
CHECK
Test every option against every clue.
5
Watch out!
The shape rule changes from question to question.
QuestionWatch forExample
Q 1You cannot rotate the images.A shape lying on its side is a different option.
Q 3Count the angles of the piece you keep.A rectangle has 4 angles before any cut.
Q 7Adjacent means sharing an edge, not just a corner.Faces that meet only at a point may share a colour.
Q 9Count the faces you cannot see.A face pressed against another cube is hidden.
Q 10Both conditions: yellow at one end, no red at the other.An edge from yellow to red does not count.

Try one first, with Dyna
Ravi's shape: (1) It has 4 sides. (2) All 4 sides are equal. (3) It has no right angle. Which shape is it?
a) Square
b) Rectangle
c) Rhombus
d) Triangle
Before you open a hint, write your plan in one line:
Hint 1 · Echo
Say it in your own words: "I need one shape that passes all 3 clues." Number the clues.
Hint 2 · Vault
What do you know? A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. A rectangle has 4 right angles.
Hint 3 · Slicer
Check one clue at a time. Clue 1 removes the triangle. Clue 2 removes the rectangle.
YOUR TURN
Two shapes are left. Use clue 3 on them. Which one has no right angle?
Use the hints one at a time. Try on your own before you read the next one.
Before you start
There is no activity in this chapter. Keep paper, scissors and a few blocks or a dice ready to try the shapes.
Challenge ahead
The Thinking Spot is a shape-placing puzzle with three rules. Keep your starting routine ready!
